To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a linear-logarithmic CMOS pixel with a programmable dynamic range has been purposely designed and fabricated for endoscopic applications and that a theoretical model of the device has been developed and validated.
a CMOS linear-logarithmic pixel with programmable DR has been designed for endoscope imaging.

we have designed and fabricated a CMOS linear–logarithmic pixel with tunable dynamic range, which has been fully characterized and tested, and which can be applied to a wide range of endoscopic applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new CMOS sensor for the visible range that can operate in a wide LIPD range with high DR, and that can be adapted to the specific requirements of different applications.
the design of a CMOS linear-logarithmic pixel, with tunable DR, based on a programmable transition point, which can be exploited in different application fields, e.g. medical endoscopy.
a new CMOS pixel that has a linear-logarithmic behavior with programmable transition point and high DR, which makes it suitable for endoscopic applications and other fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work represents a significant step toward a new generation of CMOS sensors with extended DR and reduced noise, thus paving the way for new applications.
a new pixel has been developed, characterized by linear–logarithmic response, programmable dynamic range and low noise, which has been fully validated by experimental results.
the proposed pixel is suitable for high DR applications and is a good compromise between the performance of the CMOS sensor and the performance of the photodiode sensor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pixel presented is a good candidate for applications where high DR is needed and where the light irradiation is not too high.
we have developed a CMOS pixel that is linear in the LIPD range of 0–1.2 W/cm2 and logarithmic in the range of 1.2–10 W/cm2.
the proposed architecture has the capability to achieve the best performance in terms of both noise and DR.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the architecture presented is able to provide a linear-logarithmic output signal with a wide dynamic range, thus allowing the design of a smart camera with a single pixel array and a single readout circuit.
the architecture is suitable for applications in which the LIPD is known a priori, e.g., for endoscopy and industrial automation, and can be used to obtain an extremely wide range of DR.
a pixel with tunable transition point and logarithmic compression can be used in a large range of applications, including those in which the LIPD is not known in advance.
